title: Leaked ICE Emails Reveal U.S.-Iran Coordination on Deportation Flights During Wartime
excerpt: Hundreds of internal emails show American immigration officials worked with Iranian government representatives to deport over 100 Iranians, with Tehran influencing who was put on the planes.
body:
• Newly released internal ICE emails reveal U.S. immigration officials coordinated with Iranian government representatives to arrange three deportation flights carrying over 100 Iranians back to Tehran in September 2025, December 2025, and January 2026.
  • Iranian officials had direct influence over deportation lists, with ICE staff adding names "per request from the Iran Embassy" and making last-minute manifest changes at Tehran's direction.
  • The deportation push was labeled a "White House priority" and continued even during the 12-day U.S.-Iran war in June 2025, when Iranian airspace was closed and Iranians were fleeing the country.
  • A federal lawsuit alleges ICE illegally shared confidential asylum application details with Iranian officials, potentially endangering deportees upon return. DHS denies the allegations.

Emails Reveal a Quiet Channel

Hundreds of internal emails exchanged between U.S. immigration officials paint the most detailed picture yet of how Washington and Tehran — two governments without formal diplomatic relations since 1979 — quietly worked together to deport Iranian nationals from American soil.

https://x.com/Newsforce/status/2090539286483402971

The emails, obtained by the National Iranian American Council (NIAC) and made public on Tuesday, show that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement coordinated with Iranian government officials to arrange more than 100 deportations on three separate flights routed through Qatar in September 2025, December 2025, and January 2026, according to the Associated Press.

The flights included political activists and members of ethnic and religious minorities who expressed concerns about returning to Iran, a country whose government has a documented pattern of violent persecution against women, dissidents, and minority groups, according to The Intercept.

Iran's Influence Over the Lists

The emails reveal that Iranian officials had direct sway over who ended up on deportation flights. "Per request from the Iran Embassy I added a few cases," one unnamed ICE official wrote in late August 2025, a month before the first flight departed.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=d3sw1gfB7aY

"Iran has requested that I amend the previous manifest and expedite the removal process."

— Unnamed ICE official, in internal email

Just over a week later, another official with the same job title made further changes after meeting with the "Director at the Iranian Embassy." Three days before the September 29 departure, Iranian officials were still requesting additions. On the day the flight left, last-minute requests were denied, but by then the coordination pattern was well established.

At least one person was deported who was not supposed to be on the flight. "An Iranian not included on the final manifest we sent to the Qatari MOI was boarded on the flight," an ICE official wrote. A colleague responded: "I have no idea how the case/person got through on the plane." The individual was ultimately sent to Iran.

Deportations Continued During War

The emails show that deportation planning remained a top priority even as the United States and Iran exchanged military strikes during a 12-day conflict between June 13 and June 24, 2025. Just days after President Trump posted on social media that "Everyone should immediately evacuate Tehran!" former acting ICE Director Todd Lyons called the repatriation of Iranians a "priority" in an email to removal operations head Marcos Charles, according to AP.

Charles forwarded the directive and ordered staff to develop a plan for deporting 58 Iranians with final removal orders in ICE custody.

"We need a plan forward ASAP."

— Marcos Charles, ICE head of removal operations

Officials warned that "removal will prove difficult" because Iran was not issuing travel documents and its airspace was closed during the bombings. Another official urged colleagues to "identify a solution for this White House priority."

Asylum Information Allegedly Shared

A federal lawsuit filed in July by the Iranian American Legal Defense Fund alleges that ICE went further than logistics coordination — sharing confidential asylum application details with Iranian government officials, in violation of federal regulations passed in the late 1990s specifically to protect asylum seekers from persecution upon return.

Eleven Iranians in immigration detention submitted sworn declarations stating they were forced to meet with Iranian government officials while in ICE custody, and that those officials "had knowledge of their immigration cases, including the details of their asylum applications," according to court filings reviewed by CNN.

The Department of Homeland Security has denied the allegations. "These allegations that ICE shared asylum application records with the Iranian government are FALSE," DHS said in a statement.

What It Means for Immigrants

For the estimated 600 Iranians placed in immigration detention last year, the revelations raise acute concerns. The deportation flights mark a sharp departure from decades of U.S. policy welcoming Iranian dissidents and exiles since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.

"It demonstrates that the top priority here was to kick out as many people as possible by whatever means necessary," said Jamal Abdi, president of the NIAC.

The case has significant implications for the broader Indian and South Asian diaspora watching U.S. immigration enforcement evolve under the Trump administration, particularly as deportation cooperation agreements expand to countries with which the U.S. has had limited diplomatic engagement.

What's Next

The federal lawsuit remains active in a Washington, D.C., court. The newly released emails are expected to strengthen plaintiffs' arguments that the government violated confidentiality protections. DHS has not commented on the latest batch of emails. Congress has not announced any hearings on the matter, but immigration advocacy groups are calling for a full investigation into the coordination between ICE and Iranian authorities.
nri_angle: The U.S.-Iran deportation coordination raises concerns across immigrant communities about expanded enforcement cooperation with countries that may persecute returnees, with implications for asylum seekers from multiple regions.
